requirements.quote:
A Handshake packet uses long headers with a type value of 0x02,
   followed by the Length and Packet Number fields; see Section 17.2.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a long header whose packet type value is 0x02, with the Length and Packet Number fields following it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a Handshake packet with a short header, a different packet type value, or without the stated following fields.
requirements.why_checkable: The header form, type bits, and subsequent field placement can be inspected in the serialized packet.

requirements.quote: The first byte contains the Reserved and Packet Number Length bits;
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the first byte of a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Reserved bits and Packet Number Length bits in the first byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit these bit fields from the first byte.
requirements.why_checkable: Their presence and positions can be checked directly in the first encoded byte.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 1-bit Header Form field with value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a Header Form value other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The fixed-width field and its fixed value can be checked from the wire representation.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 1-bit Fixed Bit field with value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a Fixed Bit value other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit value is directly observable in the encoded header.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 2-bit Long Packet Type field with value 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a Long Packet Type value other than 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and fixed value are directly testable in serialized packets.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a 2-bit Reserved Bits field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode this field at a width other than 2 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and location can be validated against the packet layout.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a 2-bit Packet Number Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode this field at a width other than 2 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width can be verified from the header layout.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a 32-bit Version field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the Version field at a width other than 32 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is directly testable in a serialized header.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include an 8-bit Destination Connection ID Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode this length field at a width other than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is directly observable in the wire representation.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Destination Connection ID with a length from 0 through 160 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a Destination Connection ID longer than 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection ID's encoded bit length can be measured and checked against the bound.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include an 8-bit Source Connection ID Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode this length field at a width other than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is directly observable in the wire representation.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Source Connection ID with a length from 0 through 160 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a Source Connection ID longer than 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection ID's encoded bit length can be measured and checked against the bound.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Length field using the indicated variable-length integer encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: Presence and encoding of the Length field can be checked in a serialized packet, though details of the variable-length encoding are defined elsewhere.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Packet Number field with a width from 8 through 32 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the Packet Number outside the 8-to-32-bit width range.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Packet Number width can be measured directly.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Packet Payload of at least 8 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode an empty or sub-8-bit Packet Payload.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload presence and length can be measured in the encoded packet.

requirements.quote:
Once a client has received a Handshake packet from a server, it uses
   Handshake packets to send subsequent cryptographic handshake messages
   and acknowledgments to the server.
requirements.condition: Once a client has received a Handshake packet from a server and subsequently sends cryptographic handshake messages or acknowledgments to that server.
requirements.required_behavior: Use Handshake packets for those subsequent cryptographic handshake messages and acknowledgments.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send those subsequent messages or acknowledgments using a different packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can correlate receipt of the server's Handshake packet with the packet type used for later client handshake messages and acknowledgments.

requirements.quote:
The Destination Connection ID field in a Handshake packet contains a
   connection ID that is chosen by the recipient of the packet; the
requirements.condition: When sending a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Destination Connection ID to a connection ID chosen by the packet recipient.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place a connection ID not chosen by the recipient in the Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field value can be compared with the set of connection IDs issued or selected by the recipient.

requirements.quote:
Source Connection ID includes the connection ID that the sender of
   the packet wishes to use; see Section 7.2.
requirements.condition: When sending a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Source Connection ID to the connection ID that the packet sender wishes to use.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field can be compared with the sender's selected local connection ID.

requirements.quote: Handshake packets have their own packet number space, and thus the
requirements.condition: When assigning or tracking packet numbers for Handshake packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain a packet number space dedicated to Handshake packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not share the Handshake packet number space with other packet-number spaces.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state and packet traces can show whether Handshake packet numbers are tracked independently.

requirements.quote:
Handshake packets have their own packet number space, and thus the
   first Handshake packet sent by a server contains a packet number of
   0.
requirements.condition: When a server sends its first Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set its packet number to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign a nonzero packet number to the server's first Handshake packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The first server Handshake packet in a trace can be identified and its decoded packet number compared with zero.

requirements.quote:
The payload of this packet contains CRYPTO frames and could contain
   PING, PADDING, or ACK frames.  Handshake packets MAY contain
   CONNECTION_CLOSE frames of type 0x1c.
requirements.condition: When constructing a Handshake packet payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Include CRYPTO frames; PING, PADDING, ACK, and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames of type 0x1c are also permitted.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type other than 0x1c under this permission.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame parsing can determine whether CRYPTO is present and whether every additional frame is one of the enumerated permitted types.

requirements.quote:
CONNECTION_CLOSE frames of type 0x1c.  Endpoints MUST treat receipt
   of Handshake packets with other frames as a connection error of type
   PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a Handshake packet containing a frame other than CRYPTO, PING, PADDING, ACK, or CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or process the packet as valid.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inject each disallowed frame type into a Handshake packet and observe the resulting connection error code.

requirements.quote:
Like Initial packets (see Section 17.2.2.1), data in CRYPTO frames
   for Handshake packets is discarded -- and no longer retransmitted --
   when Handshake protection keys are discarded.
requirements.condition: When Handshake protection keys are discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard data from CRYPTO frames carried in Handshake packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain that CRYPTO-frame data after discarding the Handshake protection keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state can be inspected after key discard to verify removal of retained Handshake CRYPTO data.

requirements.quote:
Like Initial packets (see Section 17.2.2.1), data in CRYPTO frames
   for Handshake packets is discarded -- and no longer retransmitted --
   when Handshake protection keys are discarded.
requirements.condition: After Handshake protection keys are discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Stop retransmitting data from CRYPTO frames carried in Handshake packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retransmit that data after Handshake protection-key discard.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet trace after key discard can verify that the affected CRYPTO data is never retransmitted.
